glm.feedback:
Findings:

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-adopt/scripts/tools/generate_adoption_artifacts.py:131–133 (and plugin_signal.py:28)
  Finding: The `claude-plugin` runtime key is a matching signal, not a version, but it is written into the same `stack.runtime` dict whose values every other consumer treats as "<tool> version: <version>". `_extract_constraints` special-cases it, but any other reader of `stack.runtime` in the snapshot (brief generators, docs writers, downstream tooling) will render it as e.g. "Claude-plugin version: .claude-plugin/". Only one consumer is patched.
  Suggestion: Either namespace the signal outside `runtime` (e.g. `stack.plugin_signal`), or grep the codebase for other `stack["runtime"]` consumers and skip the key there too. Also bump `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` since the runtime shape changed.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-project/tests/test_claude_plugin_profile_select.py:12–16
  Finding: `test_bundled_claude_plugin_profile_can_be_selected_by_name` only calls `check_profile`, which validates the name against the resolver — the test's own docstring concedes "nothing is special-cased". It would pass for any existing profile name and doesn't demonstrate that `/shipwright-project` (the interview listing) actually surfaces `claude-plugin` to the user.
  Suggestion: Add an assertion against the profile-listing path the skill uses (e.g. that `claude-plugin` appears in the offered names), so a regression in listing wouldn't slip through.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-adopt/scripts/lib/plugin_signal.py:24–26
  Finding: `stack.setdefault("signals", []).append(SIGNAL)` appends without deduplication; if `analyze` were ever re-run on an already-annotated stack (or the signal logic is reused on a cached snapshot), the signal appears twice. Harmless today because `analyze` runs it once, but fragile.
  Suggestion: Guard with `if SIGNAL not in stack["signals"]` before appending.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-adopt/tests/test_profile_matcher.py:73
  Finding: `assert result["confidence"] >= 0.30` pins an arbitrary internal threshold; the AC only requires the generic profile still matches. If the matcher's confidence scale changes, this test breaks for a non-defect.
  Suggestion: Drop the numeric threshold and assert only the match and score ordering (which is the actual AC).

Spec compliance: AC30–AC32 all appear implemented — the profile validates, Python data matches the generic profile, adopt fixtures cover both branches end-to-end (including the full `analyze` path), and mechanism paths are checked for existence and hook registration. Docs and CI/CodeQL wiring are updated consistently.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes; the work is sound and well-tested, but the `claude-plugin` key leaking into `stack.runtime` for unpatched consumers is worth cleaning up before merge.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
